title: Pressure-cooker white rice
subtitle: Perfectly cooked basmati in 6 minutes
excerpt: Basmati rice cooked under pressure with the absorption method. Separate, fluffy, non-sticky grains every time, with none of the risk of a scorched or gluey base.
sourceNotes: Pressure-cooking white rice using the absorption method is documented across South Asian, Persian, and American electric pressure cooker recipe literature. The method eliminates the risk of boiling over or uneven cooking that stovetop rice can produce.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze in airtight bags for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in a saucepan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Cook a double batch and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Cold cooked rice is ideal for fried rice.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Refrigerate cooked rice for up to 4 days. Note: rice must be cooled rapidly and refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking.

content.text: Pressure-cooker white rice uses the absorption method. The rice takes in exactly as much water as it needs. Six minutes at pressure gives a reliable, consistent result. The sealed pot stops evaporation, so the ratio stays right every time.
Rinse the rice before cooking. This removes surface starch that would otherwise make the grains clump together. Three rinses under cold water, until the water runs mostly clear, is enough.
The natural pressure release is the second half of the cooking. Do not skip it or shorten it, the steam inside the pot finishes the rice after the heat goes off. Allow the full 10 minutes.

Put the rinsed rice in the pressure cooker. Add cold water in a 1:1.25 ratio, 300 g of rice requires 375 ml of water. Add salt and stir once. Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 3 minutes. Allow a natural pressure release of 10 minutes. Do not quick-release.
Open the lid. The rice should have absorbed all the water. Fluff with a fork and serve immediately.

rows.symptom: The rice is wet and sticky
rows.cause: Too much water was added, or the rice was not rinsed.
rows.fix: Return the open pot to low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, uncovered, to drive off excess moisture. For next time, rinse the rice and use exactly 1.25 parts water to 1 part rice.

rows.symptom: The rice is dry at the bottom and wet on top
rows.cause: The lid was opened before the natural release completed.
rows.fix: Seal the lid and leave for the remaining natural release time before opening.

rows.symptom: The bottom layer is slightly scorched
rows.cause: The cooker reached pressure too aggressively, or the base was too hot during sauté.
rows.fix: Bring to pressure gently over medium heat rather than high. Do not use sauté mode before adding the rice water.

content.text: Basmati rice is the go-to side for curries, dals, grilled meats, and a dozen other dishes. The pressure cooker version is useful for batch cooking, double the quantity, cool rapidly, and refrigerate for up to four days. Day-old refrigerated rice is the best starting point for fried rice, which requires cold, dry grains rather than freshly cooked sticky ones.
